chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
O son of Adam, do not carry the worry of the day that has not yet come upon the day that has already come, for if that day is from your lifespan, Allah will bring your provision in it.

key_terms.يَوْمِكَ: your day (referring to a specific period of time or life stage)

ai.seo_question: How to manage anxiety about the future according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this maxim from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) addresses the human tendency toward excessive worry about future sustenance, urging believers to anchor their trust in Allah's timely provision. This teaching aligns with the Shia concept of *Tawakkul* (reliance on God), emphasizing that anxiety is unnecessary because Allah's knowledge encompasses all days, and He will send forth the provision for each day when it arrives. It serves as a practical spiritual remedy for *Ham* (burden/anxiety), encouraging mindfulness of the present moment while maintaining faith in divine timing.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 267. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
O’ son of Adam, do not inflict the worry of the day that has not yet come on the day which has already come, because if that day be in your life Allāh will bestow its livelihood also.
